# BK7258 phase-one Armino baseline build.
#
# Spec: docs/compose/spec/bk7258-wifi-native.md, S2.2 and task T8.
#
# Compiles the CP units of the Armino iperf baseline unchanged, from the
# manifest generated by chips/bk7258/tools/armino_compile_manifest.py. Each
# Armino component becomes one static library with that component's own
# baseline flags, so the final link pulls in only referenced members, as the
# baseline link does with --start-group/--gc-sections.

if(CONFIG_BK7258_WIFI_ARMINO_BASELINE)

  # Phase one compiles the Armino baseline unchanged. T19 imported the
  # compiled units, their include closure and the closed archives into
  # chips/bk7258/armino_baseline/ (see its PROVENANCE.md), so a clean
  # checkout builds with no local Armino tree. The variable remains as an
  # override for regenerating the manifest from a real baseline checkout
  # (tools/armino_compile_manifest.py).
  if(NOT BK7258_ARMINO_BASELINE_DIR AND DEFINED ENV{BK7258_ARMINO_BASELINE_DIR})
    set(BK7258_ARMINO_BASELINE_DIR "$ENV{BK7258_ARMINO_BASELINE_DIR}"
        CACHE PATH "Armino baseline tree compiled by BK7258_WIFI_ARMINO_BASELINE")
  endif()
  if(NOT BK7258_ARMINO_BASELINE_DIR)
    set(BK7258_ARMINO_BASELINE_DIR "${CMAKE_CURRENT_SOURCE_DIR}/../armino_baseline")
  endif()
  if(NOT IS_DIRECTORY "${BK7258_ARMINO_BASELINE_DIR}/cp")
    message(FATAL_ERROR
      "BK7258_WIFI_ARMINO_BASELINE: no Armino tree at "
      "'${BK7258_ARMINO_BASELINE_DIR}' (want cp/ beneath it)")
  endif()

  set(manifest ${CMAKE_CURRENT_SOURCE_DIR}/../tools/armino_baseline)

  # The manifest records one baseline commit (its first line). The imported
  # tree is byte-identical to it by armino_source_gate.py, so no runtime
  # commit check is needed here.
  file(STRINGS ${manifest}/component_flags.tsv flag_rows)

  # Components left out of phase one, with the evidence required by S2.7:
  # os_source is the FreeRTOS kernel (one scheduler only, NuttX's);
  # lwip_intf_v2_1 is replaced by NuttX's own TCP/IP stack (user decision).
  set(excluded os_source lwip_intf_v2_1 bk_cli at_server)

  # lwip's buffer and utility units are gone too. bk_wifi uses them as its
  # packet buffer (pbuf), buffer allocator and address helpers -- none is
  # protocol code, and none of their symbols is defined by NuttX -- and all
  # six now come from compat/bk7258_netbuf.c on one private SRAM arena:
  #
  #   src/core/pbuf.c           pbuf_alloc/free/ref/header/cat/copy/coalesce
  #   src/core/mem.c            the arena, with mem.c's API kept
  #   src/core/memp.c           nothing: PBUF_POOL requests are arena blocks
  #   src/core/def.c            lwip_htons()/lwip_htonl()
  #   src/core/ipv4/ip4_addr.c  ip4addr_aton()/ip4addr_ntoa()/_r()
  #   src/core/stats.c          lwip_stats, a zero-initialised struct
  #
  # Two reasons, both measured on the board. Memory: pbuf.c, memp.c and
  # stats.c cost ~23 KiB of .bss for a PBUF_POOL nothing allocates, plus
  # mem.c's 50 KiB MEM_SIZE arena; the replacement is one arena sized by the
  # frame it has to hold. Placement: pbuf memory must be SRAM (the MAC's TX
  # DMA cannot read PSRAM), which neither lwip unit can promise.
  #
  # The include directories and lwip_os/lwip_compat headers stay: Armino
  # sources and compat/*.c still include lwip/pbuf.h and lwip/mem.h. Nothing
  # from the lwip component is compiled now, so there is no exception list.

  # Single units left out because NuttX owns the OS interface they provide
  # (S2.7): pthread TLS (its only callers are the excluded lwip and
  # os_source), and the bk_patch signal stubs (empty bodies, now static
  # inline in compat/bk_patch/signal.h).
  set(excluded_units
      # The six lwip units compat/bk7258_netbuf.c replaces (see the lwip note
      # above). Removing these lines restores the stock lwip packet buffer.
      cp/components/lwip_intf_v2_1/lwip-2.1.2/src/core/pbuf.c
      cp/components/lwip_intf_v2_1/lwip-2.1.2/src/core/mem.c
      cp/components/lwip_intf_v2_1/lwip-2.1.2/src/core/memp.c
      cp/components/lwip_intf_v2_1/lwip-2.1.2/src/core/def.c
      cp/components/lwip_intf_v2_1/lwip-2.1.2/src/core/ipv4/ip4_addr.c
      cp/components/lwip_intf_v2_1/lwip-2.1.2/src/core/stats.c
      cp/components/bk_rtos/freertos/posix/freertos_impl/source/pthread_local_storage.c
      cp/components/wpa_supplicant-2.10/bk_patch/signal.c
      # shell_uart.c drove UART0, which NuttX owns.  The shell device driver
      # that used to stand in for it is gone too: components/bk_cli no longer
      # builds (it had no input device left), and compat/bk7258_armino_shell_api.c
      # provides the log/assert entry points the remaining archives call.
      # cli_rpc.c's only used export was cli_debug_cmd_table.
      cp/components/bk_cli/shell_uart.c
      cp/components/bk_cli/cli_rpc.c
      # Reset belongs to NuttX: the Armino reset entry, and SystemInit which
      # only it calls. set_reboot_tag() moves to bk7258_armino_start.c.
      cp/components/cmsis/CMSIS_5/Device/Beken/bk7236xx/Source/startup_bk7236.c
      cp/components/cmsis/CMSIS_5/Device/Beken/bk7236xx/Source/system_bk7236xx.c
      # MBOX0 belongs to NuttX's RPMsg transport: chips/bk7258/mb_ipc/
      # bk_mailbox_rpmsg.c provides every global of mbox0_adapter.c, and
      # mbox0_drv.c is only used by the adapter.
      cp/middleware/driver/mailbox/mbox0_adapter.c
      cp/middleware/driver/mailbox/mbox0_drv.c
      # The NVIC belongs to NuttX: the bk_int_* API, Armino's own NVIC
      # driver and its vector handlers are replaced by
      # compat/bk7258_armino_irq.c.
      cp/middleware/driver/icu/interrupt_base.c
      cp/middleware/arch/cm33/arch_interrupt.c
      cp/middleware/driver/bk7258/interrupt.c
      # TRNG belongs to the chip layer: chips/bk7258/bk7258_trng.c provides
      # the same six symbols (bk_trng_driver_init/deinit, bk_trng_start/stop,
      # bk_rand, bk_fill_rand) with the baseline's semantics. trng_hal.c and
      # trng_ll.c are only used by trng_driver.c, so the whole unit goes.
      # cli_trng.c stays: it is a caller of those symbols, not a provider.
      cp/middleware/driver/trng/trng_driver.c
      cp/middleware/soc/common/hal/trng_hal.c
      cp/middleware/soc/bk7258/hal/trng_ll.c
      cp/middleware/soc/bk7258/hal/trng_hal_debug.c
      # GPIO belongs to the chip layer: chips/bk7258/bk7258_gpio.c is the
      # single owner of the AON GPIO block (SOC_AON_GPIO_REG_BASE ==
      # BK7258_AON_GPIO_BASE == 0x44000400).  Keeping both left two drivers
      # writing the same registers -- uart_driver.c's bk_gpio_pull_up/down
      # raced our own bk7258_gpio_uart0 on the same pins.  gpio_hal.c and
      # gpio_ll.c follow in the next step: their only callers were these two.
      cp/middleware/driver/gpio/gpio_driver_base.c
      cp/middleware/driver/bk7258/gpio_driver.c
      # gpio_hal.c is the other direction of the same block: the Armino hal
      # API that remaining baseline units call (pm.c's
      # gpio_hal_switch_to_low_power_status on sleep entry).  Its 27 symbols
      # now come from chips/bk7258/bk7258_gpio_hal.c, same bodies, same
      # gpio_ll inlines, same GPIO_DEV_MAP / usr_gpio_cfg tables.  gpio_ll.c
      # follows: it only ever provided inlines to these two.
      cp/middleware/soc/common/hal/gpio_hal.c
      cp/middleware/soc/bk7258/hal/gpio_ll.c
      # The UART register layer: chips/bk7258/bk7258_uart_hal.c provides the
      # same 10 symbols on the authority's uart_ll.h inlines.  uart_driver.c
      # stays for now -- it is the 57-symbol driver face and is the next step.
      cp/middleware/soc/common/hal/uart_hal.c
      # The driver face above it: chips/bk7258/bk7258_uart_driver.c provides
      # the same 57 symbols with the same #if gates.  Only seven of them are
      # live in this image (boot init, two gpio queries, the two PM stubs, the
      # pm-id mapping and uart_wait_tx_over) -- the rest lost their callers
      # when the Armino CLI lost its input device and logging moved to syslog.
      cp/middleware/driver/uart/uart_driver.c
      # SYS touch face: chips/bk7258/bk7258_sys_touch_driver.c provides the
      # same 22 register wrappers.  None of them is referenced today.
      cp/middleware/driver/sys_ctrl/sys_touch_driver.c
      # The audio half of the same sysctrl face: chips/bk7258/
      # bk7258_sys_audio_driver.c provides the same 42 wrappers, byte for
      # byte, including the two that hold the analog resource around the write.
      cp/middleware/driver/sys_ctrl/sys_audio_driver.c
      # The stack-reading half of the exception dump: chips/bk7258/
      # bk7258_stack_base.c provides the same 3 symbols (code_addr_is_valid,
      # stack_mem_dump, arch_parse_stack_backtrace).  None of them is
      # referenced today; the writing half stays in trap_base.c.
      cp/middleware/arch/cm33/stack_base.c
      # The driver bring-up itself: chips/bk7258/bk7258_driver.c provides
      # driver_early_init/driver_init with the authority's call list, order and
      # #if gates.  Both bodies are byte-identical to this unit's, including
      # the local PSRAM bring-up the baseline already carried here.
      cp/middleware/driver/common/driver.c
      # The exception and dump core: chips/bk7258/bk7258_trap_base.c provides
      # the same 22 symbols -- the Peterson lock in the shared SRAM area, the
      # per-core interrupt-enable snapshots, the emergency UART writer and the
      # assert/crash dump paths.  Every body is carried with its #if gates;
      # it is compiled with the baseline's -fsigned-char so the char handling
      # matches too.
      cp/middleware/arch/cm33/trap_base.c
      # The CM33 core face: chips/bk7258/bk7258_arm.c provides the same 9
      # symbols (arch_init/smem_reset_lastblock are empty in the authority and
      # stay empty; the rest is the WFI, NVIC-pending and LDREX/STREX set).
      cp/middleware/arch/cm33/arm.c
      # The device model table and its dispatch: chips/bk7258/
      # bk7258_drv_model.c provides the same 12 symbols.  All twelve bodies
      # and the DD_MAX_DEV-slot table are byte-identical to this unit's.
      cp/middleware/driver/common/drv_model.c
      # The device-driver init table: chips/bk7258/bk7258_dd.c provides
      # g_dd_init/g_dd_exit.  Its table is empty in this configuration
      # (CONFIG_SOC_BK7236XX selects the small table, and its only entry needs
      # CONFIG_FLASH_ORIGIN_API), so both bodies are the authority's empty
      # walk -- byte for byte.
      cp/middleware/driver/common/dd.c
      # The touch controller driver was only kept in the image by cli_pwr.c's
      # bk_touch_register_touch_isr() call.  With components/bk_cli gone that
      # reference is gone too, so the whole unit drops out without a port:
      # this board never drives the panel path.
      cp/middleware/driver/touch/touch_driver_v1_1.c
      # The log transport: chips/bk7258/bk7258_printf.c provides the same 26
      # symbols (printf 20 + printf_base 6) with the provider's format and
      # filters, but hands every line to syslog instead of the UART driver.
      # shell_task.c stays: libbk_phy still references shell_log_flush().
      cp/components/bk_system/printf.c
      cp/components/bk_system/printf_base.c
      # Timer belongs to the chip layer for the same reason: chips/bk7258/
      # bk7258_timer.c owns TIMER_ID0..5 (SOC_TIMER0_REG_BASE ==
      # BK7258_TIMER0_BASE == 0x44810000) and now supplies bk_timer_* too.
      # rosc_ppm's TIMER_ID0 is the channel /dev/timer0 uses, so two drivers
      # were writing the same enable and end-count registers.
      cp/middleware/driver/timer/timer_driver.c
      cp/middleware/soc/common/hal/timer_hal.c
      # T14 third slice: the flash command layer itself (read/write/erase,
      # status register, protection state machine, cross-core bracketing).
      # chips/bk7258/bk7258_flash_driver.c provides the same 30 symbols,
      # byte for byte.
      cp/middleware/driver/flash/flash_driver.c
      # T14 second slice: the partition table and its access checks.
      # chips/bk7258/bk7258_flash_partition.c provides the same 9 symbols,
      # byte for byte; this is the layer an mtd_partition table would come from.
      cp/middleware/driver/flash/flash_partition.c
      # T14 first slice: the flash register layer.  chips/bk7258/
      # bk7258_flash_hal.c provides the same 2 symbols, byte for byte.
      cp/middleware/soc/common/hal/flash_hal.c
      # The AON RTC driver: chips/bk7258/bk7258_aon_rtc.c provides the same 16
      # symbols (two 64-bit units, tick/upper comparators, the per-unit alarm
      # list, the two ISR entry points and the wake-source registration) with
      # every #if gate carried.  Only the __LINE__ constants in two log/assert
      # messages differ from the authority object.
      cp/middleware/driver/rtc/aon_rtc_driver_64bit.c
      # The register layer under it, already replaced (see below).
      # The AON RTC register layer: chips/bk7258/bk7258_aon_rtc_hal.c provides
      # the same 28 wrappers on the authority's aon_rtc_ll.h inlines.  The
      # driver unit above it (aon_rtc_driver_64bit.c) is the next step, and
      # stays until then.
      cp/middleware/soc/common/hal/aon_rtc_hal_64bit.c
      cp/middleware/soc/bk7258/hal/timer_ll.c
      cp/middleware/soc/bk7258/hal/timer_hal.c
      cp/middleware/soc/bk7258/hal/timer_hal_debug.c
      # WDT and reset-reason belong to the chip layer: chips/bk7258/
      # bk7258_wdt.c provides the same 30 symbols (wdt_driver 17,
      # aon_wdt_driver 5, wdt_hal 5, aon_wdt_hal 3) and
      # chips/bk7258/bk7258_reset_reason.c the remaining 13 (reset_reason
      # 11, reboot 2). The signatures still come from these units' own
      # headers and the register layer from wdt_ll.h / aon_wdt_ll.h, so
      # the port keeps the authority's #if gates, key sequences and wall
      # clock time base. cli_wdt.c / cli_misc.c stay: they are callers,
      # not providers.
      cp/middleware/driver/wdt/wdt_driver.c
      cp/middleware/soc/common/hal/wdt_hal.c
      cp/middleware/driver/aon_wdt/aon_wdt_driver.c
      cp/middleware/soc/common/hal/aon_wdt_hal.c
      cp/middleware/driver/reset_reason/reset_reason.c
      cp/components/bk_system/reboot.c
      # Temperature and voltage detection belongs to the chip layer:
      # chips/bk7258/temp_detect/bk7258_temp_detect.c provides the same 26
      # symbols (temp_detect 10, bk_sensor 7, volt_detect 9) with the
      # authority's bodies.  cli_temp_detect.c stays: it is a caller.
      cp/components/temp_detect/temp_detect.c
      cp/components/temp_detect/bk_sensor.c
      cp/components/temp_detect/volt_detect.c)

  # driver.c is excluded (chips/bk7258/bk7258_driver.c is its port), so the
  # CONFIG_SPI collision it needed this list for is handled inside that file
  # instead: NuttX's config.h defines CONFIG_SPI for its own SPI layer, while
  # the Armino name means "the Armino SPI driver is built", which it is not.
  set(nuttx_config_compat_components "")

  # bk_patch holds wpa's own headers plus a bare-metal signal.h that shadows
  # NuttX's <signal.h>. Replace its -I with: generated forwarders for the
  # wpa-own headers, and compat/bk_patch for signal.h.
  set(bk_patch_dir "${BK7258_ARMINO_BASELINE_DIR}/cp/components/wpa_supplicant-2.10/bk_patch")
  set(bk_patch_fwd "${CMAKE_CURRENT_BINARY_DIR}/bk_patch_fwd")
  foreach(h bk_vsie_cus.h ddrv.h errno-base.h fake_socket.h sk_intf.h wpa_err.h)
    file(WRITE ${bk_patch_fwd}/${h}.tmp "/* Generated: forwards to the baseline bk_patch header. */\n#include \"${bk_patch_dir}/${h}\"\n")
    file(COPY_FILE ${bk_patch_fwd}/${h}.tmp ${bk_patch_fwd}/${h} ONLY_IF_DIFFERENT)
    file(REMOVE ${bk_patch_fwd}/${h}.tmp)
  endforeach()
  set(bk_patch_replacement
      "-I${bk_patch_fwd}" "-I${CMAKE_CURRENT_SOURCE_DIR}/compat/bk_patch")

  # wifi_spinlock.h is reached by same-directory includes, so it is replaced
  # by forcing a header that defines its guard first. Components from the
  # baseline ninja deps log.
  set(spinlock_compat_components bk_wifi wpa_supplicant-2.10)

  # lwip is excluded, but kept components still carry its bare header
  # directory, which shadows NuttX's own errno.h, netdb.h, debug.h and err.h
  # for NuttX headers too. Replace it, in place, with lwip_compat: it forwards
  # only the lwip-only names the baseline resolved there (ninja deps log),
  # and leaves the POSIX names to NuttX.
  set(lwip_bare_dir
      "-I${BK7258_ARMINO_BASELINE_DIR}/cp/components/lwip_intf_v2_1/lwip-2.1.2/src/include/lwip")
  set(lwip_src_include
      "-I${BK7258_ARMINO_BASELINE_DIR}/cp/components/lwip_intf_v2_1/lwip-2.1.2/src/include")

  # ram_regions.h is force-included by the baseline for 38 components, and
  # that copy is generated for the baseline SRAM split: CONFIG_PWR_MNG_ADDR
  # is 0x2805db00 there, while this board puts PWR_MNG at 0x2809f700
  # (bk7258_memorymap.h). bk_pm_module_lv_sleep_state_get/clear and
  # pm_debug_lv_state read that address, so without this replacement they
  # touch AP RAM (0x2805db00 falls inside the AP window). pm/nuttx_port/
  # include/ram_regions.h re-exports the board values instead. Same pattern
  # as lwip_compat above: replaced in place, not by editing the manifest.
  set(baseline_ram_regions
      "-include${BK7258_ARMINO_BASELINE_DIR}/build/bk7258/iperf/partitions/ram_regions.h")
  # The same baseline directory is also on -I and provides two headers:
  # ram_regions.h, which pwr_clk.h includes by name (so it must not be
  # found there, or the later include undoes the forced one above), and
  # partitions_gen.h, which partitions.h needs. Put our own ram_regions.h
  # first and keep the baseline directory behind it for the rest.
  set(baseline_partitions_dir
      "-I${BK7258_ARMINO_BASELINE_DIR}/build/bk7258/iperf/partitions")
  set(nuttx_ram_regions
      "-include${NUTTX_CHIP_ABS_DIR}/pm/nuttx_port/include/ram_regions.h"
      "-DCONFIG_BK7258_RPMSG_SHM_ADDR=${CONFIG_BK7258_RPMSG_SHM_ADDR}")
  set(nuttx_ram_regions_dirs
      "-I${NUTTX_CHIP_ABS_DIR}/pm/nuttx_port/include"
      "-I${NUTTX_CHIP_ABS_DIR}/include")

  foreach(row IN LISTS flag_rows)
    if(row MATCHES "^#" OR row MATCHES "^component\t")
      continue()
    endif()
    string(REPLACE "@ARMINO@" "${BK7258_ARMINO_BASELINE_DIR}" row "${row}")
    string(REPLACE "\t" ";" fields "${row}")
    list(POP_FRONT fields comp)
    list(FIND fields "${baseline_ram_regions}" ram_regions_index)
    if(ram_regions_index GREATER_EQUAL 0)
      list(REMOVE_AT fields ${ram_regions_index})
      list(INSERT fields ${ram_regions_index} ${nuttx_ram_regions})
    endif()
    list(FIND fields "${baseline_partitions_dir}" partitions_index)
    if(partitions_index GREATER_EQUAL 0)
      list(REMOVE_AT fields ${partitions_index})
      list(INSERT fields ${partitions_index}
           ${nuttx_ram_regions_dirs} ${baseline_partitions_dir})
    endif()
    list(FIND fields "${lwip_bare_dir}" bare_index)
    if(bare_index GREATER_EQUAL 0)
      list(REMOVE_AT fields ${bare_index})
      list(INSERT fields ${bare_index} "-I${CMAKE_CURRENT_SOURCE_DIR}/lwip_compat")
    endif()
    # lwip_os replaces the lwip headers that redefine OS interfaces
    # (sockets.h, inet.h) or collide with a NuttX macro (stats.h); it must
    # come before lwip's own src/include so "lwip/..." resolves to it.
    list(FIND fields "${lwip_src_include}" src_include_index)
    if(src_include_index GREATER_EQUAL 0)
      list(INSERT fields ${src_include_index} "-I${CMAKE_CURRENT_SOURCE_DIR}/lwip_os")
    endif()
    list(FIND fields "-I${bk_patch_dir}" patch_index)
    if(patch_index GREATER_EQUAL 0)
      list(REMOVE_AT fields ${patch_index})
      list(INSERT fields ${patch_index} ${bk_patch_replacement})
    endif()
    if(comp IN_LIST nuttx_config_compat_components)
      list(APPEND fields -include ${CMAKE_CURRENT_SOURCE_DIR}/compat/bk7258_armino_nuttx_config.h)
    endif()
    if(comp IN_LIST spinlock_compat_components)
      list(APPEND fields -include ${CMAKE_CURRENT_SOURCE_DIR}/compat/bk7258_wifi_spinlock.h)
    endif()
    # The lwip component's flag set -- lwip's include closure with lwip_os
    # first, plus compat/bk7258_lwip_compat.h -- is now what
    # compat/bk7258_netbuf.c compiles with. The compat header undefines
    # getopt's opterr for lwip's stats struct and declares pbuf_debug_flag.
    if(comp STREQUAL "lwip_intf_v2_1")
      list(APPEND fields -DPBUF_POOL_FREE_OOSEQ=0
           -include ${CMAKE_CURRENT_SOURCE_DIR}/compat/bk7258_lwip_compat.h)
    endif()
    # The chip include root mirrors the baseline layout (driver/wdt.h,
    # driver/aon_wdt.h, ...), so putting it first makes those paths resolve to
    # the nativized headers.  A header only lands there after the
    # preprocessing comparison shows it declares the same contract as the
    # baseline copy.  Insert into the list, never into a joined string -- the
    # fields are processed as a list below.
    list(INSERT fields 0 "-I${NUTTX_CHIP_ABS_DIR}/include")
    set(flags_${comp} "${fields}")
  endforeach()

  set(components)
  file(STRINGS ${manifest}/armino_units.tsv unit_rows)
  foreach(row IN LISTS unit_rows)
    if(row MATCHES "^component\t")
      continue()
    endif()
    string(REPLACE "\t" ";" fields "${row}")
    list(GET fields 0 comp)
    list(GET fields 1 src)
    list(GET fields 3 file_define)
    if(comp IN_LIST excluded OR src IN_LIST excluded_units)
      continue()
    endif()
    set(src ${BK7258_ARMINO_BASELINE_DIR}/${src})
    list(APPEND srcs_${comp} ${src})
    list(APPEND components ${comp})
    if(NOT file_define STREQUAL "-")
      set_source_files_properties(${src} PROPERTIES COMPILE_OPTIONS "${file_define}")
    endif()
  endforeach()
  list(REMOVE_DUPLICATES components)

  # The packet buffer (compat/bk7258_netbuf.c) and the SRAM arena behind it
  # (compat/bk7258_netheap.c), in place of the six excluded lwip units.
  # Libraries of their own for the same two reasons as the other compat
  # units: they need lwip's flag set, which is per component, and they must
  # NOT go through the allocator renaming below -- they never call a C
  # allocator.
  nuttx_add_kernel_library(armino_netheap
                           ${CMAKE_CURRENT_SOURCE_DIR}/compat/bk7258_netheap.c)
  target_compile_options(armino_netheap PRIVATE ${flags_lwip_intf_v2_1})
  nuttx_add_kernel_library(armino_netbuf
                           ${CMAKE_CURRENT_SOURCE_DIR}/compat/bk7258_netbuf.c)
  target_compile_options(armino_netbuf PRIVATE ${flags_lwip_intf_v2_1})


  # The baseline links with -Wl,--wrap for the C allocator (build.ninja), so
  # every Armino and closed-library malloc goes through bk_rtos/
  # platform_stub.c: __wrap_malloc -> os_malloc -> pvPortMalloc, which hands
  # out zeroed memory (compat/bk7258_freertos_nuttx.c), and the closed
  # libraries rely on that. A global --wrap would also reroute NuttX's own
  # allocator calls, so the same renaming is applied to Armino code only:
  # to each Armino library once it is archived, and to build-tree copies of
  # the closed archives. Only names platform_stub.c wraps are listed; no
  # Armino unit defines any of them. Board boot 2026-10-03 faulted in
  # sta_mgmt_init() on a 0x55555555 list pointer from libwifi's unwrapped
  # malloc.
  set(alloc_wrap ${CMAKE_CURRENT_BINARY_DIR}/armino_alloc_wrap.syms)
  file(WRITE ${alloc_wrap}.tmp
       "malloc __wrap_malloc\ncalloc __wrap_calloc\nrealloc __wrap_realloc\n"
       "free __wrap_free\nzalloc __wrap_zalloc\n_malloc_r __wrap__malloc_r\n"
       "_calloc_r __wrap__calloc_r\n_realloc_r __wrap__realloc_r\n"
       "_free_r __wrap__free_r\n")
  file(COPY_FILE ${alloc_wrap}.tmp ${alloc_wrap} ONLY_IF_DIFFERENT)
  file(REMOVE ${alloc_wrap}.tmp)

  foreach(comp IN LISTS components)
    string(MAKE_C_IDENTIFIER "armino_${comp}" target)
    nuttx_add_kernel_library(${target} ${srcs_${comp}})
    target_compile_options(${target} PRIVATE ${flags_${comp}})
    add_custom_command(
      TARGET ${target} POST_BUILD
      COMMAND ${CMAKE_OBJCOPY} --redefine-syms=${alloc_wrap}
              $<TARGET_FILE:${target}>
      VERBATIM)
  endforeach()

  # The closed archives on the baseline app.elf link line (build.ninja),
  # renamed as above into the build tree; the baseline tree is not touched.
  set(closed_dir ${CMAKE_CURRENT_BINARY_DIR}/closed_libs)
  file(MAKE_DIRECTORY ${closed_dir})
  foreach(lib libwifi libbk_phy libbk_coex libbk_phy_info libble_wifi_exchange libuid)
    set(src ${BK7258_ARMINO_BASELINE_DIR}/cp/components/bk_libs/bk7258/libs/${lib}.a)
    set(dst ${closed_dir}/${lib}.a)
    set_property(DIRECTORY APPEND PROPERTY CMAKE_CONFIGURE_DEPENDS ${src} ${alloc_wrap})
    if(NOT EXISTS ${dst} OR ${src} IS_NEWER_THAN ${dst} OR ${alloc_wrap} IS_NEWER_THAN ${dst})
      execute_process(
        COMMAND ${CMAKE_OBJCOPY} --redefine-syms=${alloc_wrap} ${src} ${dst}
        RESULT_VARIABLE objcopy_result)
      if(NOT objcopy_result EQUAL 0)
        message(FATAL_ERROR "objcopy failed on ${src}: ${objcopy_result}")
      endif()
    endif()
    nuttx_add_extra_library(${dst})
  endforeach()

  # Temporary connection entry until wlan0 has wireless ops (spec S2.9).
  nuttx_add_application(
    NAME armino_sta
    SRCS ${CMAKE_CURRENT_SOURCE_DIR}/bk7258_armino_sta.c
    STACKSIZE 4096)

  target_sources(arch PRIVATE bk7258_armino_start.c
                 compat/bk7258_armino_shell.c compat/bk7258_armino_irq.c
                 compat/bk7258_armino_shell_api.c
                 compat/bk7258_freertos_nuttx.c compat/bk7258_lwip_sys.c
                 compat/bk7258_armino_netdev.c
                 compat/bk7258_armino_wops.c)

  # The wext control-plane adapter is the one file that has to see both
  # worlds: it takes NuttX's iwreq and calls Armino's STA/scan entry
  # points, so it needs modules/wifi.h for those types.  set_property
  # with TARGET_DIRECTORY because the source goes into `arch`, whose
  # directory scope is not this one (set_source_files_properties would
  # not apply).  Scoped to this one file so the Armino include root does
  # not shadow headers for the rest of arch.
  set_property(SOURCE "${CMAKE_CURRENT_SOURCE_DIR}/compat/bk7258_armino_wops.c"
               TARGET_DIRECTORY arch
               APPEND PROPERTY COMPILE_OPTIONS
               "-I${BK7258_ARMINO_BASELINE_DIR}/cp/include")

endif()
